paragraphs.text: # dsh-activity-heat · Recent Activity
> A DeepSeek Harness plugin that surfaces **the sessions and workspaces you most recently talked to*
*, using a heat score derived from elapsed time — so the conversation you just had never gets buried
, using a heat score derived from elapsed time — so the conversation you just had never gets buried.
English | 中文
## Why
Sessions pile up in the DSH sidebar, nested inside workspace groups. The one you just spoke in is pu
shed out of sight within minutes.
This plugin computes a 0–100% heat score from **time since last activity** and expresses it in three
places plus a panel — the more recent, the more visible.
## What you see
| Where | What it does |
| **Sidebar entry** | A heat-ring icon whose brightness follows the hottest session in the profile |
| **Session title** | A small dot before the title text: solid = warm/blazing, hollow = active and
cooler. Cold sessions are grey, hotter ones turn blue; active sessions pulse gently; hidden after 7

days. The row-leading cell stays with the host's state dot and the schedule clock |
| **Session hove
r card** | `Heat 4/5 · Warm`, `Last active: 40 min ago`, `This workspace is hot`; the status line is
rendered natively by the host (Running / Waiting for approval / Plan review / Waiting for answer /

Completed / Idle) |
| **Main panel** | Sessions / Workspaces views, each with heat filters and a cou

dle) |
| **Main panel** | Sessions / Workspaces views, each with heat filters and a count selector |
### Panel

- **Top-level switch**: `Sessions 58` / `Workspaces 10` — no more mixed list
- **Two-row toolbar, on
e material**: the panel draws no title. The **primary row** holds the Sessions/Workspaces switch, th
e range switch (Active / Archived / Subagents), and a right-aligned count picker labelled *Count* wi
th Select. The **filter row** is its own line: heat bands as pill chips with a count badge, horizont
ally scrollable. Every control shares **one glass surface** (translucent fill + hairline border + to
p highlight); the active state only layers blue fill/border/text on that same glass, so hierarchy co
mes from accent strength alone — never a mix of solid white blocks, bare text and solid blue pills.

- **Count selector**: sessions `10 / 20 / 30 / 50`, workspaces `5 / 10 / 20`
- **Heat filter**: All

/ Blazing / Warm / Active / Recent / Stale, with live counts
- **Every card**: the bottom row is spl
it into three groups divided by hairlines — ① cache hit rate + context usage (each with a mini progr
ess bar) ② turns + steps + tokens ③ accumulated conversation time; items inside a group use a dot, g
roups are separated by a vertical rule. The `Current` state is a badge before the title, and the rel

ative time lives in the right column, not the meta row.
- **Session status (native-aligned)**: Runni
ng / Waiting for approval / Plan awaiting review / Waiting for answer / Completed / Idle, all drawn
with the host `StateDot` (blue spinner / amber dot / green dot / grey dot). The data source is the h
ost `useSessionStatus` (`running` / `pendingInteraction` / `completionUnread`); “N subagents running
” stacks alongside the primary state. Waiting states and Completed drop the running frame; only Runn

ing keeps it.
- **Token breakdown**: hovering the token figure opens a details card — exact total, c
ache hit rate, uncached input, cached input, cache write (when non-zero) and output, mirroring the h

ost's "Token usage" dialog
[该节后续省略]
### Right-click menu
Right-click a session card (or focus it and press `Shift+F10` / the Menu key):
| Action | Notes |

| Open session | Same as clicking the card |
| Open in terminal | Opens the session/workspace direct
ory in the system terminal: Windows tries Windows Terminal → PowerShell 7 → Windows PowerShell; macO

S uses Terminal; Linux uses x-terminal-emulator |
| Open in… | Two-level cascading menu (hover subme
nu in the panel; the native sidebar row menu expands the same submenu on hover — no second click). T
he first row is always "Open in terminal"; the rest list locally probed file managers / editors / te

rminals (including Git Bash and WSL); picking one opens the session/workspace directory there |
| Co
py session ID / title / latest prompt / working directory | The latest prompt is copied in full; cli

pboard failures are reported |
| Pin / unpin | Writes the host sidebar order; this panel keeps sorti

ng by heat |
| Rename… | Prefilled with the current title; an empty title cannot be saved |
| Fork s

ession | Creates a branch at the last completed turn without navigating |
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
- Turns, tokens, cache hit rate and context usage read `sessionStats`, `tokenUsage` and `contextPres
sure` — the same projections as the composer status bar, so the numbers match it exactly. Profiles t
hat only expose `contextTimeline` fall back to its values; in that case the figures can differ from

the status bar.
- No Linux default shortcut is declared; Linux users bind one in Settings.
- The rig
ht-click menu does **not** delete sessions: the host only supports archiving, and archived sessions

can be restored from the sidebar's archived view.
- Running sessions' archive item becomes “Stop and
archive…”: the dialog lists the running turn / subagents / jobs / schedules and stops them (irrever

sible) before archiving; the panel re-sorts by heat afterwards.
- "Download session log" requires th
e host to mount `dsh-session-log-export`; without it the item reports unavailability instead of open

ing a 404 page.
- The host's native sidebar rows expose no right-click event, but they do expose `si
debar.workspaces.session.menu.item` / `.row.action` seats; the plugin's terminal / copy / download a
ctions live there, while pin / rename / fork / archive use the host's own items and the central pane

l keeps the full menu.
- `updatedAt` is the host's last-activity snapshot and does not refresh with
tool steps or streaming output; the panel treats running sessions as maximum heat, which does not me

an they just received a message.
- "Open in…" is implemented by the plugin's own Host routes: `GET /
activity-heat/open-with/apps` probes installed apps that can open a directory (Windows: `App Paths`
registry + common install paths + PATH; macOS: `.app` bundles; Linux: `xdg-open`), and `POST /activi
ty-heat/open-with/open` launches with the target directory and reports the real outcome. The list is

cached for 60s; if probing fails it falls back to the host `open-in-app/apps`.
[该节后续省略]
